narratives.Overview:
## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/polynomial-redos` — Polynomial regular expression used on uncontrolled data.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#114](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/114) |
| Rule | `js/polynomial-redos` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/docs/docs-impact.ts` ~L115 |
| Message | This regular expression that depends on library input may run slow on strings starting with 'surfaces:' / 'surfaces:a' and with many repetitions of ' '. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/polynomial-redos` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#114](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/114) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #114.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #114 flags SURFACES_RE in docs-impact.ts because /^surfaces:\s*(.+)\s*$/im can backtrack on uncontrolled PR-body input that starts with 'surfaces:' and repeats spaces. Prefer-A rewrites that capture away from the (.+)\s*$ ambiguity so alert #114 clears by a real fix. Changing CodeQL suite config or suppress-as-primary stays a keep-out.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. Rewrite SURFACES_RE so the surfaces: line is parsed without greedy (.+) plus trailing \s* on the same match (for example capture the remainder of the line then trim, or an equivalent non-ambiguous line parse). Keep parseDeclaredSurfaces / parseDocsImpactDeclaration behavior for none and kind:id lists.
2. Add adversarial coverage for long space-padded / surfaces:-prefix strings that previously stressed the ReDoS shape; existing docs-impact unit tests stay green.
3. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #114 / #5743.
4. Keep-out: CodeQL suite-config / path-exclude / suppress as the primary fix (issue Non-goals).

## Reject (draft)
- Treating CodeQL config / suppress / dismiss-without-fix as the primary remedy
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue
- Changing CHANGE_CLASS_RE / RATIONALE_RE / declaration semantics beyond what SURFACES_RE rewrite requires
- Claiming alert #114 cleared without a tip rewrite (or an evidence-backed false-positive disposition after review)

## file_scope lean (draft)
packages/core/src/docs/docs-impact.ts (+tests as needed); CHANGELOG.md.

Prefer-A survives refutation as a direction: fix the parser, keep suite configuration and suppression out of the primary remedy. Two findings sharpen the binding scope; neither requires a broader parser redesign.

Verification: pin-read the dispatched docs-impact.ts, docs-impact.test.ts, and Critic method / Stop 5 contract; read issue body and comments 6256504732, 6256514353, 6256518896 only. Static verification, not a runtime benchmark or CodeQL rerun. I have not independently established alert clearance.

Existing mechanisms: parseDeclaredSurfaces already trims the captured value, recognizes none, splits comma-separated tokens, and filters kinds/empty ids. parseDocsImpactDeclaration distinguishes a missing surfaces match from an empty parsed list. evaluateDocsImpact already refuses omitted touched surfaces and false no-impact declarations. REST transport uses execFileSync with timeout/maxBuffer; --body-file reads a string directly before synchronous parsing. These are existing controls, not gaps requiring new infrastructure.

### F1 — sharpens-framing — Specify the compatibility boundary before choosing a line-only extraction

Evidence: at the dispatch SHA, SURFACES_RE is /^surfaces:\s*(.+)\s*$/im. Its leading \s* includes line terminators. Thus a body fragment spelled `surfaces:\ncommand:foo` can capture command:foo from the following line. Conversely, bare `surfaces:` at EOF has no match because .+ requires a character. parseDeclaredSurfaces trims, but cannot restore either distinction after extraction. The pinned declaration tests cover normal values and missing fields, not these boundary cases.

Failure mode: “capture the remainder of the line then trim” can change cross-line acceptance or turn a previously missing field into an accepted empty list. A rewrite may pass every existing test while contradicting the draft's promise to preserve parseDocsImpactDeclaration behavior. This matters for untrusted PR text: field boundaries determine which text supplies the declared surface set.

Disposition consequence: the lean can bind with an explicit compatibility statement and fixtures for bare/whitespace-only fields, next-line values, duplicate fields, LF/CRLF and JavaScript line separators, plus ordinary none and kind:id lists. Preserve existing behavior deliberately, or name the narrow intentional boundary change; do not describe a strict line parser as automatically equivalent. Keep the existing declared-versus-touched control.

### F2 — sharpens-framing — Define performance evidence separately from functional examples and alert closure

Evidence: the pinned transport timeout surrounds gh/git child processes, not SURFACES_RE.exec(body); the body-file path has no equivalent transport bound. RATIONALE_MAX_CHARS is checked after regex execution and does not bound the surfaces input. The existing tests assert parsing and gate outcomes; they do not demonstrate adversarial runtime behavior. The draft proposes long padded inputs but names neither a replacement expression nor a complexity argument.

Failure mode: a long successful match may be fast while another input shape remains expensive. Passing a single padding example, or observing a passing unit suite, therefore does not establish that P1 is relieved. A synchronous regex also cannot reliably be interrupted by a timer running on the same event loop.

Disposition consequence: retain the narrow rewrite, but require inspection of the complete replacement for overlapping repetitions and repeated suffix scans, adversarial cases covering both accepted and rejected inputs, and current-tip CodeQL evidence for alert #114. If executable timing checks are used, put potentially hanging probes in a separately killable process with a generous external deadline; do not rely on a same-thread test timeout or brittle millisecond threshold. Report functional compatibility, runtime evidence, and eventual master alert closure separately.

Injection / swarm lens: PR-body text remains data. The concrete exposure here is parser resource consumption and field-boundary interpretation, not authority to execute instructions in that text. No new shared-state or worker protocol is needed.

Road not taken: a hard body-size cap could bound exposure, but adds a rejection policy and compatibility cost beyond removing ambiguity at the flagged site. Suppression would become defensible only with evidence establishing a false positive under the actual supported runtime/input path; that evidence is absent from this pinned review. Neither alternative displaces Prefer-A.

**Lean:** Prefer-A — rewrite SURFACES_RE away from (.+)\s*$ ambiguity; lock line-boundary compatibility + adversarial/CodeQL evidence; keep suite-config suppress out.

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #114 is a real parser ReDoS shape on SURFACES_RE. Prefer-A clears it by rewriting the surfaces: line parse, not by silencing CodeQL. Codex Round-1 accepted the direction and sharpened two binding obligations: name the line-boundary compatibility contract (so a rewrite does not silently change next-line / bare-field behavior), and separate functional fixtures from performance/alert-closure evidence.

## Bound remedy
1. **relieves: P1 — Rewrite SURFACES_RE off (.+)\\s*$ ambiguity.** Replace /^surfaces:\s*(.+)\s*$/im with a non-ambiguous surfaces: line parse (remainder-of-line then trim, or equivalent). Preserve parseDeclaredSurfaces / parseDocsImpactDeclaration outcomes for ordinary none and kind:id lists. Keep evaluateDocsImpact declared-versus-touched control unchanged.
2. **relieves: P1 — Lock line-boundary compatibility fixtures (Codex F1).** Before or with the rewrite, record an explicit compatibility statement and fixtures for: bare/whitespace-only surfaces: fields; next-line values under current leading-\\s* behavior; duplicate surfaces: fields; LF/CRLF (and JS line-separator) line ends; ordinary none and kind:id lists. Preserve existing behavior deliberately, or name any narrow intentional boundary change — do not claim a strict line parser is automatically equivalent.
3. **relieves: P1 — Adversarial + CodeQL evidence (Codex F2).** Add adversarial accepted and rejected inputs that stress the old (.+)\s*$ shape. Inspect the complete replacement for overlapping repetitions / repeated suffix scans. Report functional compatibility, runtime evidence, and master alert #114 closure as separate evidence rows. If executable timing probes are used, run them in a separately killable process with an external deadline — not a same-thread millisecond assert. Tip CodeQL evidence for alert #114 is required for ship closure.
4. **relieves: P1 — CHANGELOG Security/Fixed for alert #114 / #5743.**

### Reject
- CodeQL suite-config / path-exclude / suppress / dismiss-without-fix as the primary remedy
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts
- Broader parser redesign beyond SURFACES_RE / surfaces: line parse
- Hard PR-body size cap as the primary P1 control (Codex road-not-taken)
- Claiming P1 relieved from a single padding example or green unit suite alone
- Changing CHANGE_CLASS_RE / RATIONALE_RE / declaration semantics beyond what the SURFACES_RE rewrite requires

### Disposition of Round-1
- Codex F1 (sharpens-framing) -> accept-into-contract as limb 2
- Codex F2 (sharpens-framing) -> accept-into-contract as limb 3
- Prefer-A direction survives; empty disagreement set on blocks-the-design

Verification was static source inspection under the specified pin-read path, not a benchmark, replacement implementation, or CodeQL run. No comments above the ceiling were read.

P1 coverage: the pinned parser executes SURFACES_RE directly on the supplied body before the rationale-length check. parseDeclaredSurfaces trims and filters tokens only after extraction; it cannot bound regex work. Bound limb 1 removes the ambiguous extraction itself, and limb 3 requires inspection of the complete replacement for overlapping repetitions and repeated suffix scans, accepted and rejected adversarial cases, and separate runtime and CodeQL evidence. These obligations address the resource-consumption mechanism rather than merely silencing its report. The separately killable-process requirement makes any executable timing probe meaningful despite synchronous parsing.

The predecessor findings are absorbed. Limb 3 separates functional compatibility, runtime evidence, and master alert closure, with tip CodeQL evidence required for ship closure. Neither finding needs reopening.

Existing controls remain adequate for their distinct purpose: parseDeclaredSurfaces filters recognized kinds and nonempty ids; evaluateDocsImpact checks declared versus touched surfaces and rejects false no-impact declarations. Retaining those controls prevents the resource fix from weakening the declaration gate. PR-body text remains untrusted data; this remedy changes its extraction cost and boundary handling, not its authority.

A hard body-size cap could limit exposure, but would introduce a separate rejection policy and is unnecessary to this narrow remedy. No new control or broader parser redesign is needed to cover the named P1.
